chapter_title_ka: ხვარაზმშას შვილის ინდოეთს მოსლვა საქორწილოდ და ტარიელისაგან მისი მოკლვა
chapter_title_en: Arrival of the Khwarazmsha's Son in India for the Wedding and his Slaying by Tariel
chapter_expert_explanation_en: When the Khwarazmian prince arrives and pitches his tents, Tariel rides at night with a hundred men, enters the tent, and slays the bridegroom cleanly without shedding the blood of his sleeping retinue, then fortifies himself in his city and sends word to King Parsadan that he will never allow a foreign prince to usurp the Indian throne.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
მოვიდა კაცი: “სასიძო მოვაო” , მოსლვა გვახარა,
მაგრა თუ ღმერთი რას უზამს, არა იცოდა, გლახ, არა;
მეფესა მიჰხვდა სიამე, არ სიტყვა ივაგლახა რა,
და მიბრძანა, ახლოს მიმისვა, “მოდიო”, თავი დახარა.
stanzas.english_translation: "A man came. 'The bridegroom cometh,' announced he but, wretched man! he knew not what God was preparing for him. The king looked pleased, he spoke no woeful words; he bade me sit near him; 'Come,' said he, and inclined his head.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 25 ('Arrival of the Khwarazmsha's Son in India for the Wedding and his Slaying by Tariel', Stanza 548; Wardrop Stanza 532): Part of the narrative sequence in which when the Khwarazmian prince arrives and pitches his tents, Tariel rides at night with a hundred men, enters the tent, and slays the bridegroom cleanly without shedding the blood of his sleeping retinue, then fortifies himself in his city and sends word to King Parsadan that he will never allow a foreign prince to usurp the Indian throne.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“მიბრძანა: “ჩემთვის ესე დღე ლხინი და სიხარულია.
გარდავიხადოთ ქორწილი, ხამს ვითა დასა, სრულია;
კაცი გავგზავნოთ, მოიღონ ყოვლგნით საჭურჭლე სრულია,
და უხვად გავსცემდეთ, ვავსებდეთ, სიძუნწე უმეცრულია”.
stanzas.english_translation: "He said to me: 'For me this is a day of joy and merriment. Let us celebrate the wedding, since it is necessary that the matter he concluded; let us send a man, let us have all the treasures brought from every part, generously let us distribute, let us fill them (with treasure); avarice is clownishness.'
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 25 ('Arrival of the Khwarazmsha's Son in India for the Wedding and his Slaying by Tariel', Stanza 549; Wardrop Stanza 533): Part of the narrative sequence in which when the Khwarazmian prince arrives and pitches his tents, Tariel rides at night with a hundred men, enters the tent, and slays the bridegroom cleanly without shedding the blood of his sleeping retinue, then fortifies himself in his city and sends word to King Parsadan that he will never allow a foreign prince to usurp the Indian throne.

stanzas.english_translation: "I sent in all directions men carrying treasure. The bridegroom also came, they were no laggards; our men met them from inside, from outside came the Khvarazmians; the sum of their soldiers could not be contained even by the fields.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 25 ('Arrival of the Khwarazmsha's Son in India for the Wedding and his Slaying by Tariel', Stanza 550; Wardrop Stanza 534): Part of the narrative sequence in which when the Khwarazmian prince arrives and pitches his tents, Tariel rides at night with a hundred men, enters the tent, and slays the bridegroom cleanly without shedding the blood of his sleeping retinue, then fortifies himself in his city and sends word to King Parsadan that he will never allow a foreign prince to usurp the Indian throne.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“მეფემან ბრძანა: “მოკაზმეთ კარვითა მოედანია,
გამოისვენოს სიძემან, დაყოს ცოტაი ხანია;
მუნ მისად ნახვად გავიდენ უშენოდ სპანი სხვანია,
და შენ აქა ნახენ, კმარიან იქა ნახვისად ყმანია”.
stanzas.english_translation: "The king commanded: 'Prepare the maidan with tents, let the bridegroom rest, let him tarry there a little while; the other armies can go thither without thee to see him, thou shalt see him here, go not, this will suffice for thee.'
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 25 ('Arrival of the Khwarazmsha's Son in India for the Wedding and his Slaying by Tariel', Stanza 551; Wardrop Stanza 535): Part of the narrative sequence in which when the Khwarazmian prince arrives and pitches his tents, Tariel rides at night with a hundred men, enters the tent, and slays the bridegroom cleanly without shedding the blood of his sleeping retinue, then fortifies himself in his city and sends word to King Parsadan that he will never allow a foreign prince to usurp the Indian throne.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“მოედანს დავდგი კარვები წითლისა ატლასებისა.
მოვიდა სიძე, გარდახდა, დღე ჰგვანდა არ აღვსებისა,
შეიქმნა გასლვა შიგანთა, ჯარია მუნ ხასებისა,
და დაიწყეს დგომა ლაშქართა თემ-თემად დას-დასებისა.
stanzas.english_translation: "I raised on the maidan tents of red satin. The bridegroom arrived and entered (the tent), he dismounted; it seemed not like Easter Eve; those inside began to go out, there was a host of courtiers there, the soldiers began to form in ranks according to their clans.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 25 ('Arrival of the Khwarazmsha's Son in India for the Wedding and his Slaying by Tariel', Stanza 552; Wardrop Stanza 536): Part of the narrative sequence in which when the Khwarazmian prince arrives and pitches his tents, Tariel rides at night with a hundred men, enters the tent, and slays the bridegroom cleanly without shedding the blood of his sleeping retinue, then fortifies himself in his city and sends word to King Parsadan that he will never allow a foreign prince to usurp the Indian throne.

stanzas.english_translation: "I was wearied, as is the wont of one who has done duty; tired, I turned homeward, and wished to sleep. A slave came and gave me a letter from Asmat’h the sweet: 'Come quickly! She who is like a full-grown aloe commands thee.'
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 25 ('Arrival of the Khwarazmsha's Son in India for the Wedding and his Slaying by Tariel', Stanza 553; Wardrop Stanza 537): Part of the narrative sequence in which when the Khwarazmian prince arrives and pitches his tents, Tariel rides at night with a hundred men, enters the tent, and slays the bridegroom cleanly without shedding the blood of his sleeping retinue, then fortifies himself in his city and sends word to King Parsadan that he will never allow a foreign prince to usurp the Indian throne.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“ცხენისაგან არ გარდავჰხე, წავე ფიცხლად დავმორჩილდი;
ქალი დამხვდა ნატირები, ვჰკითხე: “ცრემლსა რასა ჰმილდი?”
მითხრა: “შენი შესწრობილი ტირილსამცა ვით ავსცილდი,
და გაუწყვედლად ვით გამართლო, რაგვარადმცა გავვაქილდი!”
stanzas.english_translation: "I dismounted not; I went quickly obedient. The maiden (Asmat’h) had been weeping; I asked her: 'Why flow thy tears?' She said to me: 'Being engaged in thy defence, how can I avoid weeping? How can I justify thee unceasingly, whatever kind of advocate I may have become!'
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 25 ('Arrival of the Khwarazmsha's Son in India for the Wedding and his Slaying by Tariel', Stanza 554; Wardrop Stanza 538): Part of the narrative sequence in which when the Khwarazmian prince arrives and pitches his tents, Tariel rides at night with a hundred men, enters the tent, and slays the bridegroom cleanly without shedding the blood of his sleeping retinue, then fortifies himself in his city and sends word to King Parsadan that he will never allow a foreign prince to usurp the Indian throne.

stanzas.english_translation: "We went in, we saw her seated on a cushion, her brows puckered; the sun could not more illume the vicinage than she. I stood before her. She said to me: 'Why standest thou there? The day of battle comes--or, wert thou forsaking me, wert thou false to me and deceiving me again?'
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 25 ('Arrival of the Khwarazmsha's Son in India for the Wedding and his Slaying by Tariel', Stanza 555; Wardrop Stanza 539): Part of the narrative sequence in which when the Khwarazmian prince arrives and pitches his tents, Tariel rides at night with a hundred men, enters the tent, and slays the bridegroom cleanly without shedding the blood of his sleeping retinue, then fortifies himself in his city and sends word to King Parsadan that he will never allow a foreign prince to usurp the Indian throne.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“მე მეწყინა, აღარა ვთქვი, ფიცხლად გარე შემოვბრუნდი.
უკუ ვჰყივლე: “აწ გამოჩნდეს, არ მინდოდეს, ვისცა ვუნდი!
ქალი ომსა რაგვარ მაწვევს, აგრე ვითა დავძაბუნდი!”
და ინა მოვე, მოკლვა მისი დავაპირე, არ დავყმუნდი.
stanzas.english_translation: "I was angered, I said nothing, hastily I went out: again; I called back: 'Now shall it be seen if I did not wish it! Am I become so cowardly that a woman urges me to fight?' I went home, I concerted his slaughter, I was not idle.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 25 ('Arrival of the Khwarazmsha's Son in India for the Wedding and his Slaying by Tariel', Stanza 556; Wardrop Stanza 540): Part of the narrative sequence in which when the Khwarazmian prince arrives and pitches his tents, Tariel rides at night with a hundred men, enters the tent, and slays the bridegroom cleanly without shedding the blood of his sleeping retinue, then fortifies himself in his city and sends word to King Parsadan that he will never allow a foreign prince to usurp the Indian throne.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“ასსა ვუბრძანე მონასა: “საომრად დაემზადენით”
შევსხედით, გავვლეთ ქალაქი, არავის გავეცხადენით.
კარავსა შევე, სასიძო ვითა წვა, ზარმც-ა თქმად ენით,
და უსისხლოდ მოვკალ იგი ყმა, თუცა ხმდა სისხლისა დენით.
stanzas.english_translation: "I commanded a hundred servants: 'Prepare for battle!' We mounted, we passed through the city without, letting anyone perceive us. I went into the tent. It is a horror to tell with the tongue how the bridegroom was lying; I killed that youth without shedding of blood (? on our side), though his blood cried out as it flowed.'
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 25 ('Arrival of the Khwarazmsha's Son in India for the Wedding and his Slaying by Tariel', Stanza 557; Wardrop Stanza 541): Part of the narrative sequence in which when the Khwarazmian prince arrives and pitches his tents, Tariel rides at night with a hundred men, enters the tent, and slays the bridegroom cleanly without shedding the blood of his sleeping retinue, then fortifies himself in his city and sends word to King Parsadan that he will never allow a foreign prince to usurp the Indian throne.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“კარვის კალთა ჩახლათული ჩავჭერ, ჩავაქარაბაკე,
ყმასა ფერხთა მოვეკიდე, თავი სვეტსა შევუტაკე.
წინა მწოლთა დაიზახეს, გლოვა მიჰხვდა საარაკე,
და ცხენსა შევჯე, წამოცავე; ჯაჭვი მეცვა საკურტაკე.
stanzas.english_translation: "I cut the tangled edge of the tent, I tore it, I seized the youth by his legs and struck his head on the tent-pole. Those lying at the door cried; their lamentation was marvellous. I mounted my horse, departed, my coat of chain mail protected me.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 25 ('Arrival of the Khwarazmsha's Son in India for the Wedding and his Slaying by Tariel', Stanza 558; Wardrop Stanza 542): Part of the narrative sequence in which when the Khwarazmian prince arrives and pitches his tents, Tariel rides at night with a hundred men, enters the tent, and slays the bridegroom cleanly without shedding the blood of his sleeping retinue, then fortifies himself in his city and sends word to King Parsadan that he will never allow a foreign prince to usurp the Indian throne.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“ხმა დამივარდა, შეიქმნა ზახილი მოსაწევარი.
წამოვე, წევნა დამიწყეს; დავხოცე ჩემი მდევარი.
ქალაქი მქონდა მაგარი, მტერთაგან მოურევარი,
და მუნ შიგან შევე მშვიდობით, ამოდ იგივე მე ვარი.
stanzas.english_translation: "An alarm was raised against me; there was a cry to pursue me. I went on, they began to follow, I slew my pursuers. I had a strong city, impregnable to the foe; I reached it in safety, pleasantly, unhurt.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 25 ('Arrival of the Khwarazmsha's Son in India for the Wedding and his Slaying by Tariel', Stanza 559; Wardrop Stanza 543): Part of the narrative sequence in which when the Khwarazmian prince arrives and pitches his tents, Tariel rides at night with a hundred men, enters the tent, and slays the bridegroom cleanly without shedding the blood of his sleeping retinue, then fortifies himself in his city and sends word to King Parsadan that he will never allow a foreign prince to usurp the Indian throne.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“კაცი გავგზავნენ, ვაცნობე ყოვლგან ლაშქარსა ყველასა:
“აქა მომმართეთ, ვინცაღა ჩემსა იქმოდეთ შველასა”
არ გაწყდა მოსლვა მდევართა ღამესა დია ბნელასა,
და ჩემი რა ცნიან, სცევდიან თავებსა მათსა მრთელასა.
stanzas.english_translation: "I sent a man, I made known to all the soldiers: 'Let all who will aid me come hither!' My pursuers did not weary of coming in the depth of dark night; when they recognized me they kept their heads whole.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 25 ('Arrival of the Khwarazmsha's Son in India for the Wedding and his Slaying by Tariel', Stanza 560; Wardrop Stanza 544): Part of the narrative sequence in which when the Khwarazmian prince arrives and pitches his tents, Tariel rides at night with a hundred men, enters the tent, and slays the bridegroom cleanly without shedding the blood of his sleeping retinue, then fortifies himself in his city and sends word to King Parsadan that he will never allow a foreign prince to usurp the Indian throne.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“ცისკრად ავდეგ, შევეკაზმე, რა გათენდა ღამე დილად;
ვნახენ სამნი დიდებულნი მეფისაგან მოგზავნილად.
ებრძანა თუ: “ღმერთმან იცის, გამეზარდე ვითა შვილად,
და ჩემი ასრე რად შესცვალე სიხარული სიმძიმილად?
stanzas.english_translation: "I arose at daybreak; I apparelled myself when night dawned into morn. I saw three lords sent by the king; he sent a message, saying: 'God knows I have fostered thee like my son; why hast thou thus changed my rejoicing into heaviness?
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 25 ('Arrival of the Khwarazmsha's Son in India for the Wedding and his Slaying by Tariel', Stanza 561; Wardrop Stanza 545): Part of the narrative sequence in which when the Khwarazmian prince arrives and pitches his tents, Tariel rides at night with a hundred men, enters the tent, and slays the bridegroom cleanly without shedding the blood of his sleeping retinue, then fortifies himself in his city and sends word to King Parsadan that he will never allow a foreign prince to usurp the Indian throne.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“ხვარაზმშას სისხლი უბრალო სახლად რად დამადებინე?
თუ ჩემი ქალი გინდოდა, რად არა შემაგებინე?
მე ბერსა შენსა გამზრდელსა სიცოცხლე მაარმებინე,
და დღედ სიკვდილამდის შენიცა თავი არ მაახლებინე!”
stanzas.english_translation: "'Why didst thou make Khvarazmsha's innocent blood to fall on our house! If thou didst desire my daughter, why didst thou not tell me so? Thou hast made life distasteful to me, thine aged foster-father; thou thyself hast brought it about that thou remainest not with me till the day of my death.'
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 25 ('Arrival of the Khwarazmsha's Son in India for the Wedding and his Slaying by Tariel', Stanza 562; Wardrop Stanza 546): Part of the narrative sequence in which when the Khwarazmian prince arrives and pitches his tents, Tariel rides at night with a hundred men, enters the tent, and slays the bridegroom cleanly without shedding the blood of his sleeping retinue, then fortifies himself in his city and sends word to King Parsadan that he will never allow a foreign prince to usurp the Indian throne.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“მე შევუთვალე: “მეფეო, ვარ უმაგრესი რვალისა,
თვარა რად მიშლის სიკვდილსა ცეცხლი სირცხვილთა ალისა,
მაგრა თვით იცით, ხელმწიფე ხამს მქმნელი სამართალისა,
და მე თქვენმან მზემან მაშოროს ნდომა თქვენისა ქალისა.
stanzas.english_translation: "In answer I sent a message: 'O king, I am stronger than bronze, and this alone hinders me from being destroyed by the fire and flame of death; but, as you know, a king should be a doer of justice; by your sun! I am far from desiring your daughter.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 25 ('Arrival of the Khwarazmsha's Son in India for the Wedding and his Slaying by Tariel', Stanza 563; Wardrop Stanza 547): Part of the narrative sequence in which when the Khwarazmian prince arrives and pitches his tents, Tariel rides at night with a hundred men, enters the tent, and slays the bridegroom cleanly without shedding the blood of his sleeping retinue, then fortifies himself in his city and sends word to King Parsadan that he will never allow a foreign prince to usurp the Indian throne.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“იცით, ინდოთა სამეფო რაზომი სრა–საჯდომია!
ერთი ღა მე ვარ მემკვიდრე; ყველაი თქვენ მოგხდომია,
ამოწყდა მათი ყველაი, მამული თქვენ დაგრჩომია;
და სამარლით ტახტი უჩემოდ არავის მისახდომია!
stanzas.english_translation: "'Thou knowest how many palaces and thrones are in India; I am the sole heir left, all has fallen into your hands, all their heirs have died out, their heritage remains to you; by right the throne belongs to none but me.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 25 ('Arrival of the Khwarazmsha's Son in India for the Wedding and his Slaying by Tariel', Stanza 564; Wardrop Stanza 548): Part of the narrative sequence in which when the Khwarazmian prince arrives and pitches his tents, Tariel rides at night with a hundred men, enters the tent, and slays the bridegroom cleanly without shedding the blood of his sleeping retinue, then fortifies himself in his city and sends word to King Parsadan that he will never allow a foreign prince to usurp the Indian throne.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“ვერ გათნევ, თქვენმან კეთილმან, აწ ეგე არ–მართალია:
ღმერთმან არ მოგცა ყმა შვილი, გიზის ერთაი ქალია,
ხვარაზმშა დაჰსვა ხელმწიფედ, დამრჩების რა ნაცვალია?
და სხვა მეფე დაჯდეს ინდოეთს, მერტყას მე ჩემი ხრმალია?!
stanzas.english_translation: "'I swear by your virtue, I cannot flatter you, now this is not just: God gave thee no son; thou hast an only daughter. If thou appointedst Khvarazmsha king, what would have been left for me in exchange? Can another king be seated on the throne of India while I wear my sword?
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 25 ('Arrival of the Khwarazmsha's Son in India for the Wedding and his Slaying by Tariel', Stanza 565; Wardrop Stanza 549): Part of the narrative sequence in which when the Khwarazmian prince arrives and pitches his tents, Tariel rides at night with a hundred men, enters the tent, and slays the bridegroom cleanly without shedding the blood of his sleeping retinue, then fortifies himself in his city and sends word to King Parsadan that he will never allow a foreign prince to usurp the Indian throne.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“შენი ქალი არად მინდა, გაათხოვე, გამარიდე,
ინდოეთი ჩემი არის, არვის მივსცე ჩემგან კიდე.
ვინცა ჩემსა დამეცილოს, მისით მასცა ამოვფხვრიდე,
და სხვას მეშველსა გარეგანსა, მომკალ, ვისცა ვინატრიდე”.
stanzas.english_translation: "'I want not thy daughter, marry her, rid her of me. India is mine, to no man else will I give it; whoever contests my right, him will I cause to be uprooted from the earth; kill me! if I need any foreign helpers.'
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 25 ('Arrival of the Khwarazmsha's Son in India for the Wedding and his Slaying by Tariel', Stanza 566; Wardrop Stanza 550): Part of the narrative sequence in which when the Khwarazmian prince arrives and pitches his tents, Tariel rides at night with a hundred men, enters the tent, and slays the bridegroom cleanly without shedding the blood of his sleeping retinue, then fortifies himself in his city and sends word to King Parsadan that he will never allow a foreign prince to usurp the Indian throne.

act_title: Act II: Tariel's Chronicle of India, Love & Loss

location.desc: Homeland of King Parsadan, Princess Nestan-Darejan, and Amirbar Tariel.

key_maxim_en: Never forgetting a friend will never do us harm.
